decisions.question: The conventions say a producer's re-plan is drained like its first plan and rewrites the Delivery paragraph. Does navigation-api@v1's Delivery paragraph change?

options.label: Leave it as written
options.consequence: The paragraph keeps saying nidana.navigation.3 delivers G9 to G13 with 'its stage functions built once per call', and nidana.navigation.6 G14 to G16 and G18 to G24 with both bindings unrestricted.

options.label: Rewrite it from the entry

decisions.why: Every claim of the paragraph still holds against the re-planned gates: .2 replays G1, G4 to G8; .3 adds G9 to G13; .4 adds G17; .5 adds G25; .6 replays unrestricted. The once-per-call clause of G13 is already named in the .3 sentence (S62's touch wrote it). The entry's count claim also checks: navigation_conformance.dart has 42 named cases and navigation_executor_conformance.dart 26, registered twice by in_memory_router_test.dart, so 52. Last producing phase stays nidana.navigation.6, so no consumer edge moves.

decisions.question: bus-api@v2's Delivery paragraph names nidana.navigation only under the `contract` edge on nidana.runtime.1 and lists nidana.flutter.4 to .7 and nidana.integration under the `hard` edge on nidana.runtime.14, while the confirm says nidana.navigation.6 waits on nidana.runtime.14 for bus-api@v2's behavior. Add nidana.navigation.6 to the hard-edge parenthetical?

options.label: Leave the paragraph unchanged
options.consequence: A reader of bus-api@v2 alone sees nidana.navigation only as a contract-edge consumer; nidana.navigation.6's wait on .14 is stated in bus-testing@v2's Delivery, in the navigation plan, and is satisfied by the same producer phase.

options.label: Add nidana.navigation.6 to the hard-edge parenthetical
options.consequence: The paragraph lists every hard-edge consumer node; edits producer-written text from a consumer's confirm, which the step's write set does not name.

decisions.why: The parenthetical has read this way since S31's reconcile of nidana.runtime (v1), and S33's reconcile of nidana.navigation left it; S83 did not change nidana.navigation.6's edge. The conventions have reconcile write Delivery from the producer's confirm entries, and this step may write only what an entry names. The paragraph is not false: nidana.navigation.1's edge is the contract edge, and the parenthetical reads as examples. Signal that would have changed my mind: a consumer plan reading bus-api@v2's Delivery to decide nidana.navigation.6 needs only nidana.runtime.1. Raised for the orchestrator to carry to H23 or the next drain of nidana.runtime.

decisions.question: Steps 4 and 7: flip phase_ids or status of navigation-api@v1, bus-api@v2, bus-testing@v2 or topology-dsl@v2?

options.label: Flip none
options.consequence: navigation-api@v1 stays stable, final; the three v2 contracts stay draft, phase_ids provisional, for H16 and H23.

options.label: Flip bus-api@v2 and bus-testing@v2 to final
options.consequence: Would claim consumer phases confirmed that still cite v1 and have not been re-planned or swept.

decisions.why: A contract flips only when both sides are confirmed. After this drain: bus-api@v2 has its producer (S80) and nidana.navigation confirmed, but nidana.flutter (21 citations of bus-api@v1), nidana.integration (19), nidana.tooling.lint (15) and nidana.tooling.codegen (9) are not; bus-testing@v2 likewise lacks nidana.flutter, nidana.integration and nidana.tooling.lint; topology-dsl@v2 lacks its producer nidana.model (23 citations of topology-dsl@v1 in plan text, H23) and four consumer nodes. Whether an unchanged consumer phase of a node not re-planned counts as confirmed is H23's question, not this step's. Status cannot reach stable without phase_ids final, so step 7 has nothing to flip. navigation-api@v1's sides are unchanged: producer re-confirmed here, consumers unchanged.
evidence: grep counts of @v1 and @v2 citations in hsdd/spec/nidana.{model,flutter,integration,tooling.lint,tooling.codegen}.md
